title: Life saver
body:
I’ve struggled with recurring mental health issues, chronic pain, and chronic gastritis for 5 years now, which initially debilitated me, left me not taking care of myself, not having any routine, never brushing my teeth, never doing the bare minimum and always being stressed by school and homework. I downloaded this about 4 years ago, and it changed everything. It pulled me out of depression twice, helped me get into a rhythm of the bare minimum, I started showering more than once a week and brushing my teeth everyday, and taking my meds. It helped me see what I had to do when my mind and body failed me, and despite me not being perfect everyday, it has 100% made a difference. I’ve gone from showering every week or so, not brushing my teeth, not moving from my bed, to getting up early every day, brushing my teeth everyday, showering every other day, moving around, working, and even exercising a little bit. I’m a completely different person for better, I’m so much happier and this app has been a pivotal factor in my improvements in my health. 

Safe to say I highly recommend, but the key is not to rush perfection. It takes 28 days to change neural pathways and build habits, consistency is key, compassion is necessary. It works wonders.

title: To-Do List, Habits, Life Management
body:
Love this app, use it as a widget on my iPhone. To do lists are great, helps me stay on track so much. Love that you can see the monthly/ongoing overview for each habit so you can see how many days of the month you completed it easily. It’s really helped me with my life and it’s so good to have a portable to do list instead of keeping a million phone notes. Really user friendly and not over complicated like a lot of other organisation apps I’ve tried. (I have the paid version).
The only thing that’s annoyed me a little bit has been the inability to add ‘mood tracker’ to your daily routine without it automatically prompting you for an entry (daily) at the first opening of the app. It also adds a banner on the screen with ‘hey dear, how you feeling today…’ as another prompt to make an entry that stays there permanently unless you exit out of it. Personally I find those things a bit frustrating because they reset every day so the options are to either not have the mood tracker in your daily routine at all, or to have those notifications reset every day. It is a relatively minor thing but it does add up to be annoying if you use the app every day which I do. Only other thing coming to mind that would be a fun addition is some customisation options for widgets, like a dark option etc but that’s a SUPER minor thing and I do love the app!

title: Love this app (plus some ideas/complaints)
body:
I love this app. I have ADHD, I have tried hundreds of planner apps. I will never fully stick to a planner, but me+ is the only one I ever come back to after a procrastination hiatus.

I love the visual clarity, I love the level of customization, I love how the app is perfectly functional on the free version only, I love the features that let me track my stats, I love the badge system (bronze, gold, silver) it reminds me that even if I don’t have the motivation to do everything in a day, doing SOMETHING small is still a small win. 

I do have some minor complaints though, I hope the devs see this and implement some quality of life updates. 

Firstly, some tasks let you set a timer goal, I like this feature. My problem is the timer doesn’t work in the background when the app is closed. 

Secondly if I use a timer outwith the app, I can click on the task and pick “mark as complete” but what if I only did 10 mins out of 20. There is no way for me to put that in other than setting the in app timer, keeping the app open babysitting the timer until it hits 10 mins so I can mark stop. I really wish I was able to log manually how many minutes I did without having to use the in app timer.

Thirdly, the water tracker is a great feature, BUT if you accidentally put your water intake higher than what it actually was there’s no way to reduce the number. Sometimes this is motivating to make me reach the goals, other times it’s purely irritating because I forgot to put in yesterday’s water intake and now my stats are inaccurate.

Also, fourthly this is really really minor but worth mentioning. So, I find having an excessive number of reminders overwhelming. Instead of setting reminders on individual tasks, I create my own tasks that function as purely reminders. I set the title of these tasks as something funny but motivating for me. The problem is when the tasks show up as banner notifications on my phone, the title of the notification is usually cut off and the app creates its own body text for the notification. I’d much prefer if the body notification was just what I set the title as.

body:
I love this app and use it all day every day. But there is a MAJOR glitch. 

When deleting or amending a task and selecting ‘Just Future Task’ it deleted all the history as if you have pressed ‘Delete All’.

Not only does it erase all history or the task, it affects your percentage or the previous days and  when using this feature for organising and amending future tasks or events, it will change all of the prior inputs. 

I used the app to schedule in all netball matches at different times on a repeating task, changed the times of the matches each week and when amending the times for ‘Just future task’ it would changed the previous task too. 

Please look into this frequently used feature and try to amend the glitch. 

Thanks.

This app looked like the perfect thing for me; easy way to make a routine and stick to it, keeping track of fitness and water intake, etc. However, I couldn’t work out how to use the app. It kept getting me to do loads of things, but when I tried to save it, it would come up saying that’s need to pay for the better/full version. Also, I couldn't find anything on the app. I tried to start a custom routine but I just couldn’t find where to do that.
Overall, I think this app would be great with only a few adjustments:
- making things easier to find
- a tutorial on how to use the app?
- making most things free, but having a different version with a few added things that you need to pay for

You have a great app, why ruin it for the thousands of users who cannot afford another overpriced subscription? Get rid of the stupid pop ups.

title: Pretty good! ♡
body: This is a wonderful app, and can definitely sort out your days. Well, unless your in school. What I find troubling, is I seem to always forget to actually go on the app. I may have accidentally clicked for there to be no notifications, but I don’t think there are any. Other than this it’s a lovely app, as someone struggling to be organised, (not like I’m diagnosed with anything mental) this does help a lot. I highly recommend it to anyone with adhd or just struggle focusing, as there are daily affirmations for you to do, meditations, and so much more. Most stuff is free, but if wanted, you can buy premium and unlock a few more things! I especially love the anxiety relief meditation, after a long day of work, as I get headaches and migraines. Doing a simple 5-15 minute Excersise can seriously help you mentally and physically. Making you think more positive, and be more positive. Many children aswell will enjoy this app, it’s not a thing to show off or anything, or to be “minimalistic.” It’s a good idea, especially (I love that word haha) since it’s a day organiser, and you can choose what days certain things happen. For me, it’s school Monday-Friday. I hope the best, and cheers to the developer(s) of this absolutely game-changing app. Thank you for readying this far if you did!

body:
Me + is really, really good! It honestly structures my life on a day to day basis and helped me be organised. It motivated me with goals and criteria’s, and visually helped me using widgets and reminders. The mood tracker is great, and helps me put my day into perspective, and the endless quizzes about your life and how you can improve it are really helpful.
However…
The fact that you must buy a premium package to be able to save, edit and print pre-made routines is ridiculous, considering the price.

My suggestion…
Have a tool where you can make your own printables (routines, quotes, affirmation etc) that is completely free! Also, reduce the premium price.

All in all, a great app and I truly think that it helped me get my life in shape! 😊

title: Poorly written AI; nothing like the description
body:
I cannot figure out how this app has nearly five stars—must be bots. 
There are no routines as shown, everything has to be entered basically from scratch. There are templates, but they’re poorly written (seemingly AI generated) and unhelpful. For example, the “Home Cleanliness” routine has five steps, to be performed every day: 1-Clean the bedroom, 2-Clean the wardrobe, 3-Try changing bedroom pattern, 4-Put a pot of green plants (??), and 5-Throw away old clothes. I don’t know about you, but this routine isn’t keeping my house tidy for sure. “Keep my kitchen tidy” includes the super-helpful Tuesday task of “Clean room”. Also, “laundry [sic] the dish towels” and “sanitize the trash bins every day”. 
The 7-day free trial didn’t happen and I was charged immediately. Don’t waste your money. There are WAAAY better options out there.

You can make this in real life! For only a few pounds you could get some paper and pens to decorate to your liking. It may be free, but the advertising may get to us.

author: The Big Mahmee

title: Appreciate the concept but work is required on UX
body:
I’m a mum to one toddler (and a boyfriend to clean up after), working full time, about to start studying and so helped this app would be perfect for me trying to manage it all with my incredibly overwhelmed ADHD head of mine as starting to get burnt out. A lot of the ads I’ve seen are selling aimed at those with an ADHD diagnosis and says backed by science but there’s a couple of things that I think would just not work:
- the way the items displayed are all at once - not great for burnout and overwhelm. It mentions a few times about starting with one task yet shows you them all at once? Really there should be a toggle for the day for morning / afternoon / evening with alternate views to show all. 
- there needs to be better categorisation of tasks so you can see your cleaning, self-care, financial wellbeing, fitness, healthy eating goals better. 
- some of the suggestions for repeated tasks seem unrealistic. Like who takes trash out every day? 

All in all the idea of the app is great but just needs some refining for me to be able to use it. I could effectively just use the reminders app on iPhone if I wanted a big list of stuff.

author: What I think of me +

title: Disappointing
body:
As someone who struggles to organise my time especially in getting cleaning done efficiently…I usually blast through most of it in a day and exhaust myself so a daily, weekly and monthly rota is needed.  I downloaded this app a week ago and was so disappointed to find that it’s s blank; the user needs to input all the data themselves…one of the very things that seems a huge and impossible task for me….so I’m unable to use this huge waste of money that also tries to make me part with more money to buy their other apps.  One good thing that came out of this is that I’ve started writing a list of my tasks on paper to make a rota to stick on my fridge!  
  Come on guys, at least include a list of possible tasks  (other than vacuuming every day and changing sheets once a month WTAF!) My expectation was that there would be a list of tasks and columns of daily, weekly, monthly, bi-yearly, yearly for the user to click the task into the right column and then some blanks so the user can write in their miscellaneous tasks. 
 I think I could actually set reminders on my phone for any tasks anyway. 
By the way, I would appreciate a refund…£13 for a blank sheet (and labelled as “premium VIP”). If there is some other super duper thing that it’s supposed to do, I couldn’t find it.

author: Reviewer Of Games And Things

title: Not free, it’s £12.99 per MONTH (£156 per YEAR) after trial
body:
I was so looking forward to this having read the positive reviews. I have autism, ADHD and OCD so my organisational skills are very poor, no matter how hard I try. I have almost no sense of time due to the ADHD, and when combined with autism and OCD it makes it very difficult to address this. 

I was impressed with what I saw, until the £12.99 monthly fee (£156 per year) appeared. Whilst I understand the need to pay the staff who work hard to keep this app going, that fee is beyond ridiculous, particularly in the current economic climate. I can’t afford to feed myself and my children properly so I already miss meals to address this. Having ADHD and autism is not a lifestyle choice but a biological condition and I feel that making large amounts of money from people who genuinely struggle to cope with every day life due to no fault of their own is immoral, especially since those who are neurodiverse are the most likely to need an app such as this and are the ones who would benefit the most.

I have managed to adapt the new Apple apps which help with tasks, tracking and health to help me instead. It took several hours of my time and that of my youngest son, but we have managed to create something similar to this app across the various Apple ones, and it is FREE.  As my eldest is also autistic and has ADHD, we are trying out those apps together. It required work to set up, and will probably need a lot of tweaking, but hopefully worth it.

title: Mid App, taking advantage of ADHDers.
body:
I’m so glad I didn’t pay the subscription and used the free version, after 10mins it’s evident this app was barely thought about. 

Firstly, after entering some info and setting up, you are presented with a 2min timer and a “limited special offer” to buy a subscription. This I feel takes advantage of people like myself who suffer with ADHD a symptom of this is often having poor impulse control, when presented with a time limited offer, the app tries to capitalise on impulsivity knowing fully that the majority of its patrons are people who struggle with ADHD. They are not looking to help you, they are looking to profit from you. 
As I continue on the app suddenly a spinning roulette wheel comes up, like it would on an Asian shopping site, “congrats you have won the jackpot” 50% limited time. They knock another £10 off of the price and see if they can tempt me once more. Typical.

The app itself has a very poor interface. When setting a goal such as something simple like drinking water, you can change the measurement and value for your goal except it maxes out at 999. So if you wanted to drink more than 999ml of water in a day (there’s no litre option but you can select miles, Km or meters, if you want to drink 3miles of water as you do) then I suggest using something else.

The apps design is minimalist using emoji-esque pictures to accompany bland black and white text. It’s like it’s been made on notes and looks like any other mid tier planning app. The illustrations and guidance from a tutorial only extended to the first setting up of the app, once youre in you’re on your own, and are not given any real direction where to begin. 

Features like taking other people’s weird routines seems pointless and the options you can add are very vague and general. It doesn’t feel very personal and over all could be a much more guided experience. The whole thing seems low quality.

Also apparently they sell your data. 

Overall, it feels silly and like little effort went into this. @ developers if I get a response, I have no desire to email you with more info, your app is poor and I wish you put as much effort into helping people that you do trying to capitalise off of them. I will continue searching for an ADHD friendly planning app but the likelihood is that a good one doesn’t exist. Either way with the “limited time discounted” £17.99 yearly subscription, you should get a lot more. I’m glad I didn’t give in to my impulsiveness, the free version speaks volumes after 5 mins.

title: Good for shifting focus back to self care
body:
So far I have really enjoyed the sleep scoring, puzzle alarm, advice, soundscapes and meditation.
The habit tracker is ok, but is really hard to use if you want to be more flexible. It would be a lot better if you could set a goal of X times in a week rather than have it be a daily task. If I lived alone I might be able to pre-schedule this day is for cleaning, this day I want to do a workout, but I have to work around 4 other people’s routines and friends’ ever changing social timetables. So it’s good for little daily habits, but to track something more time consuming like a workout or getting your house in order, it lacks flexibility in its timetabling and goal setting.
My subscription is half price so for what I paid the other resources make it worth that. But if I paid full price I would be disappointed by the habit tracker part; it’s too rigid for anything other than small daily habits.

title: Brilliant!

In an era driven by technology, finding the perfect app can be a challenge. However, I am delighted to share my 5-star review on the exceptional app called Me+. With its unique features and superb functionality, Me+ has undoubtedly become a top choice for enhancing productivity, staying organized, and promoting personal growth.

Summary:
Me+ is a highly intuitive app that elevates the user's overall experience. Its sleek design and user-friendly interface provide effortless navigation, ensuring a smooth and enjoyable journey through its features. The app offers a wide range of tools that cater to various needs, from goal setting and habit tracking, to time management and personalized journaling.

Productivity at Its Best:
One of the standout features of Me+ is its ability to boost productivity by structuring tasks efficiently. With the option to create and manage multiple to-do lists, users can prioritize their tasks, set deadlines, and receive reminders. Would definitely recommend.

title: This could work 🤔
body:
I always want to be organised and clean and tidy, plus I want to develop and keep habits that use the stuff I buy, all with good intentions, only to find them still in the box months later!! 🤦‍♀️
I love lists and I’m actually quite motivated by them. 
BUT
My body has deteriorated rapidly and Co existing chronic conditions, pain and brain scrambling medications have robbed me of my ability to stick to paper or self written lists. 
This little App has certainly got off to a great start and having lists to choose from, but still edit to personalise, has been a great way to remember the things I want to do. I really enjoy ticking things off and am eager to add more things. 
The addition of different meditation programs and audible breathing techniques and fitness programs is also really great as everything is in one place. 
I’ve already learnt how to put widgets on my Home Screen with constant reminders and set a few alarms too. This way I’m being gently nudged to build the habits I want to develop and easily add them to my day. 
I’m intrigued as to how long this will last, but I bought the discounted one year package and I’m intending to enjoy and enhance my daily living with tweaks and with new goals.
